key_insight: DemoFoundry combines coding agents, physics simulation, and generative rendering to create photorealistic robot demonstrations with aligned action supervision.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces reliance on target-task human demonstrations and detailed scene appearance modeling when generating robot-training data.
method: Coding agents construct aligned real–proxy video pairs to train a video renderer.
Given a scene reference and task instruction, agents reconstruct task-relevant geometry and write executable robot-control programs.
Simulation produces proxy videos and aligned states/actions; automated checks select successful trajectories for photorealistic rendering and policy learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved visual quality and action–video consistency, with generated-data policies outperforming raw-simulation training and approaching training on an equal number of real demonstrations.
watch_item: Deployment should verify that generative rendering preserves task-critical physical interactions and action alignment across new scenes.
paper_title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
